title: US Launches AI and Quantum Computing Research for Military Logistics

content:
US launches AI and quantum computing research for military logistics.

CGI Federal, the US Defense Logistics Agency (DLA), and the University of Tennessee have launched a joint research program called Quantum Pathfinder. The initiative aims to explore how agent-based AI and quantum computing can enhance warehouse efficiency and the resilience of military supply chains. Read more.

In the initial phase, the partners will focus on three areas: dynamic management of smart warehouses, reverse logistics, and inventory distribution under disrupted infrastructure conditions. Specific use cases for these technologies are expected to be defined in the coming months.

The project is set to develop over the next fiscal year. CGI Federal will host Quantum Pathfinder at its Knoxville center, and research outcomes, including benchmarks, will be shared at industry events and through other channels.

The participants aim to leverage quantum computing and agent-based AI systems to address challenges where traditional methods face numerous variables and changing conditions. This includes restructuring logistics processes when ports, suppliers, or specific routes are unavailable. The program currently focuses on exploring potential applications rather than deploying a ready quantum system within military infrastructure.

The initiative is also linked to the development of the quantum ecosystem in Tennessee. The University plans to conduct work through the Knoxville Quantum Accelerator and the Tennessee Quantum Initiative, while simultaneously enhancing research infrastructure and training specialists.

For the DLA, this direction is not entirely new. The agency’s budget materials for the 2026 fiscal year already include plans to research quantum computing and quantum machine learning, as well as further integration of AI/ML into supply chain management processes. Read more.

Earlier, at the DefenseTalks conference in September, US Army Transportation Command General Randall Reed discussed the benefits of applying AI in military logistics.
